key: Unto Allah belong the East and the West, and whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah’s Countenance.
s: Following a warning against barring worshippers from God’s sanctuaries, the surah claims every direction for Him; al-Tabari, on 2:115, reads the naming of East and West as teaching believers that all creatures between them are His and owe Him obedience, facing wherever He directs them.
src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 2:115, the Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

evidence.words: والصواب من القول في ذلك: أن الله تعالى ذكره إنما خص الخبر عن المشرق والمغرب في هذه الآية بأنهما له ملكا، وإن كان لا شيء إلا وهو له ملك - إعلاما منه عباده المؤمنين أن له ملكهما وملك ما بينهما من الخلق، وأن على جميعهم = إذ كان له ملكهم = طاعته فيما أمرهم ونهاهم، وفيما فرض عليهم من الفرائض، والتوجهِ نحو الوجه الذي وجهوا إليه، إذْ كان من حكم المماليك طاعة مالكهم
evidence.gloss: The right view is that God singled out East and West in this ayah as His possession, though nothing is not His, to inform His believing servants that He owns them both and the creatures between them, and that all of these, being His, owe Him obedience in what He commands and forbids, in the duties He lays on them, and in turning toward the direction to which they are turned, since those owned must obey their owner.
